standard.title: Experiment with visual conventions and materials
standard.description: experiment with a range of ways to use visual conventions, visual arts processes and materials
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can experiment with materials and processes, reflect using Viewpoints questions, and use visual arts language to describe their discoveries (AC9AVA2D01). They have begun to use named visual conventions in their work. They have not yet investigated composition as a deliberate technique or documented their thinking formally.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students experiment with a range of ways to use visual conventions, visual arts processes and materials, and document and reflect on what they discover.

nodes.label: Investigating composition
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can observe and describe how artists use composition — space, balance, foreground/background, positive/negative space — in a range of artworks.
nodes.minimum_width: Examine one artwork and identify at least one compositional choice the artist made (e.g. how space is divided, where emphasis is placed).
nodes.typical_width: Examine diverse artworks to observe compositional choices; use transparent overlays or digital tools to trace dominant forms and spatial divisions; identify foreground/background, positive/negative space, and areas of emphasis.
wider: Use the compositional outline of an observed artwork as the basis for a new artwork — adapt the spatial structure while changing the subject matter or visual conventions
Compare compositional choices across artworks addressing the same theme — investigate how different compositional strategies serve different communicative purposes
nodes.hinge_reason: Composition is the structural knowledge that allows experimentation to become purposeful — students who cannot observe and name compositional choices in others' work cannot apply them deliberately in their own experimentation.

response_modes.reason: Compositional analysis is not spontaneous — students need a systematic way to look (tracing overlays, Viewpoints questions) to move beyond surface description to naming specific structural choices.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one compositional choice in an artwork (how space is used, what is emphasised)
Explains how that choice affects the meaning or experience of the work

nodes.label: Experimenting with materials and effects
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can experiment with combinations of materials and visual conventions to produce specific visual effects, working within limits and documenting discoveries.
nodes.minimum_width: Try at least two ways of combining materials or conventions to produce a visual effect; document what was tried and what resulted.
nodes.typical_width: Experiment within limits (one set of materials, one visual convention focus) to explore what combinations produce; document with annotated visual records; use Viewpoints questions to reflect on effectiveness.
wider: Explore a tactile/texture board — collect, sort and categorise materials by texture; brainstorm adjectives; invent new colour names; reflect on how materials could be used in future artworks
Try multiple printmaking approaches — use different coloured inks, add pattern and texture progressively, cut and combine elements; document how complexity increases

response_modes.reason: Experimentation with a single material type develops narrow material knowledge. The range of explorations — texture, colour, printmaking, 3D, crosshatching — each reveals different properties that enrich future making choices.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of material and process experiments available at this band (texture, printmaking, 3D, crosshatching, digital) is genuinely diverse — students who explore multiple directions build a richer material vocabulary than any single experiment allows.
success_criteria: Tries at least two ways of combining materials or conventions
Documents what was tried and what visual effect resulted

nodes.label: Documenting and reflecting
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use visual arts language to document and reflect on their experimentations — annotating what they tried, what worked, and what they would do differently.
nodes.minimum_width: Annotate at least one experiment with at least two specific comments — what was tried, what worked or didn't, and what could be explored next.
nodes.typical_width: Document experimentations with annotations, arrows and Viewpoints questions; use visual arts language accurately; reflect on effectiveness and what could be explored further; create a record that communicates learning and thinking.
wider: Create a 'work-in-progress' presentation — use audio or video annotation to accompany visual experiments, explaining the thinking and learning as it developed
Explore visual conventions used in First Nations Australian artworks — with guidance from culturally authoritative resources, document what you notice using visual arts language

response_modes.reason: Documentation habits need to be established through repeated practice at this level — the habit of annotating discoveries (not just labelling) requires consistent expectation and practice across multiple experiments.

success_criteria: Annotates at least one experiment with specific comments using visual arts language
Identifies at least one thing that could be explored or improved in future work
